name: Korea Masters
stakes: This week is crucial for India's shuttlers to gain valuable ranking points and build confidence on the international circuit, especially with the new scoring system on the horizon.
summary:
India arrives at the Korea Masters looking to build momentum, especially after a significant breakthrough on the BWF World Tour last week. While the draw for this Super 300 event is still taking shape, the focus will be on India's established stars and promising talents alike. P.V. Sindhu and Lakshya Sen will be keen to make deep runs and gather crucial ranking points, with Sindhu particularly looking to solidify her form. The men's doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, currently India's highest-ranked entry, will be aiming for consistency and another strong performance.

Adding to the buzz, young sensation Tanvi Sharma recently clinched her maiden BWF World Tour title at the Taipei Open, becoming the youngest winner in the tournament's history. While she isn't listed in the contingent for Korea, her success underscores the depth emerging in Indian badminton. Meanwhile, veteran H.S. Prannoy and the women's doubles pair of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand will also be eager to leave their mark, navigating what promises to be a competitive field. The tournament offers a valuable platform for these players to test their mettle and refine their strategies.
